title: Selenium protects neonates against neurotoxicity from prenatal exposure to manganese.
ehr_evidence: Umbilical cord blood was collected and serum was separated... Serum Mn and Se concentrations were measured by Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS)... face-to-face interviews were conducted to collect information on their socio-demographic characteristics. Neonatal Behavioral Neurological Assessment (NBNA) was administered when the infants were 3 days old
summary: A birth cohort of 933 mother-newborn pairs in Shanghai, China (2008-2009) examined whether prenatal selenium protects against manganese neurotoxicity, using umbilical cord serum Mn and Se concentrations and Neonatal Behavioral Neurological Assessment (NBNA) scores
key_findings: High Mn exposure (≥P75, 9.1 mg/L) was associated with lower NBNA score (adjusted ß = -1.2, 95% CI: -1.4 to -1.0, p<0.001) and higher risk of low NBNA (adjusted OR = 8.0, 95% CI: 2.8 to 23.0, p<0.001)

With Se <P50 (63.1 mg/L), higher cord blood Mn was negatively associated with NBNA scores (adjusted ß = -1.1, 95% CI: -1.3 to -0.9, p<0.001) and increased risk of low NBNA (adjusted OR = 5.7, 95% CI: 2.8 to 11.5, p<0.001)
The adverse effect of Mn was reduced with Se ≥P50 (63.1 mg/L) (NBNA: adjusted ß = 0.1, 95% CI: -0.3 to 0.5, p=0.746; Low NBNA: adjusted OR = 4.5, 95% CI: 0.4 to 46.7, p=0.205)
High Mn exposure group with low Se (Mn≥9.1 mg/L and Se<63.1 mg/L) had much lower NBNA scores than high Mn with high Se (38.0±1.6 vs 39.5±0.9, p<0.001)
Mn/Se ratio and NBNA scores were moderately correlated (r = -0.41, p<0.001)
captured_features: Maternal age, maternal/paternal education, maternal/paternal occupation, household income
Gestational age, birth weight, infant gender
population: 933 healthy pregnant women delivering term singleton infants (37-42 weeks gestation) and their neonates in Shanghai, China, 2008-2009
limitations: Dietary Mn and Se intake was not investigated
No long-term follow-up to assess persistent effects
Residual confounding cannot be ruled out despite adjustment for potential confounders
